examples.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^2$ over $0\le x\le4$ using two equal strips and midpoint heights.
Evaluate $\lim_{\Delta x\to0}\sum_{-2}^{3}4\,\Delta x$ using an area formula.
Evaluate $\lim_{\Delta x\to0}\sum_{1}^{4}(x+2)\,\Delta x$ using an area formula.
Evaluate $\lim_{\Delta x\to0}\sum_{3}^{8}(x-3)\,\Delta x$ using an area formula.

A car has positive velocity throughout $2\le t\le10$ seconds. Estimate how far it travels using four equal time strips and midpoint rectangles. Its velocities at $t=3$, $5$, $7$ and $9$ seconds are $7$, $10$, $15$ and $22$ m/s respectively.
examples.solution_text:
Each velocity is sampled at the midpoint of its time strip. Velocity multiplied by strip width estimates the distance travelled during that strip.
$\begin{align*}\Delta t&=\frac{10-2}{4}=2\text{ s}\\\text{Estimated distance}&=7(2)+10(2)+15(2)+22(2)\\&=108\text{ m}\end{align*}$
Because velocity is positive, the estimated change in displacement also gives the estimated distance travelled.

methods.description: Find equal strip widths and midpoints, evaluate the function at each midpoint, and sum height times width.

examples.derivation: Strip width is (4−0)/2=2; midpoints are 1 and 3. Heights are 1 and 9, so the sum is 2(1+9)=20 square units. The diagram has bases [0,2] and [2,4], heights 1 and 9, and midpoint markers on y=x².
The limit is the integral of the positive constant 4 from −2 to 3. Rectangle width is 5 and height is 4, giving 20. The diagram represents these bounds and height.
For y=x+2, endpoint heights at x=1 and x=4 are 3 and 6. The limiting area is a trapezium of width 3: 3(3+6)/2=27/2. The plotted line, endpoint labels and shaded polygon agree.
The line y=x−3 meets the axis at x=3 and has height 5 at x=8. The limiting area is a triangle with base 5 and height 5, giving 25/2. The diagram agrees.

Four strips over [2,10] have width 2 seconds and midpoints 3, 5, 7 and 9. Estimated displacement is 2(7+10+15+22)=108 metres. Positive velocity makes this the estimated distance travelled; the supplied samples suffice without a diagram.
